title: Failover: add safe-to-failover capacity checks + dependency gating
author: Benji Okafor
description: Context: The trigger engine + orchestrator state machine are now able to decide when a region is degraded/failed, but our current automation can still make a bad situation worse if we fail over into a region that is already near saturation or missing critical dependencies. This PR adds a deterministic “safe-to-failover” gate that must pass before the orchestrator can transition into progressive failover steps. What’s included: (1) Capacity gating: checks target-region GPU pool headroom, admission/dispatch queue depth, and queue age before allowing any traffic shift. (2) Dependency gating: verifies required upstream dependencies for target region are healthy (routing policy store, control plane write path, edge/DNS apply, and synthetic probe success) and that we can read the latest routing config snapshot. (3) Reasoned blocking + audit: if any gate fails, the orchestrator records a structured reason (human-readable + machine code) in the audit log and holds state in PRECHECK_BLOCKED until either signals recover or an authorized manual override is used. (4) Failure-mode tests: unit + integration tests for gate behavior (insufficient headroom, stale capacity signal, dependency unhealthy, edge apply failing) to prevent regressions. Rollout: behind FAILOVER_SAFE_TO_FAILOVER_GATES (default off). Staging will run with gates enforced; prod initial rollout will run in “observe-only” mode (audit + metrics emitted but does not block) until thresholds are tuned. Notes: Thresholds are intentionally conservative defaults; follow-up tuning will reference SLO burn + game day observations. This change is designed to reduce flappy/unsafe automation and should improve on-call confidence during regional events.
commits: 1) failover/precheck: introduce SafeToFailoverGate interface + evaluation result schema 2) capacity: add gpu_pool_headroom and queue_depth signals to precheck context 3) deps: add dependency gate (policy store, control plane write, edge apply, synthetics) 4) orchestrator: block transition w/ audit reason + hold-down behavior for precheck failures 5) tests: add failure-mode coverage for capacity + deps gates (unit + integration) 6) metrics: emit failover_precheck_* counters and structured logs
changed_areas: Core: failover-orchestrator precheck pipeline, capacity signal client, dependency health client, audit log reason codes. Tests: orchestrator integration tests, capacity signal stubs, dependency health fake server. Config: safe-to-failover thresholds + staleness windows; feature flag wiring.
snippet:
New precheck evaluation (simplified):

- CapacityGate
  - require gpu_pool_headroom_tokens_per_sec >= min_headroom_tps
  - require queue_depth_p95 <= max_queue_depth
  - require queue_age_seconds_p95 <= max_queue_age_s
  - require signal_age_seconds <= max_signal_staleness_s

- DependencyGate
  - require policy_store_read == OK
  - require control_plane_write == OK
  - require edge_apply == OK (dry-run or no-op apply depending on env)
  - require synthetic_probe_success_rate >= min_synthetics_ok

If any gate FAILs -> transition to PRECHECK_BLOCKED, emit failover_precheck_blocked_total{reason_code=...}, write audit entry with reason_code + details.
conversation: Mina Haddad (review): Can we be explicit about which queue metric we’re using? I don’t want us to block failover because a single route/model backlog spikes. Benji Okafor (author): Good call. I changed the capacity gate to use region-level admission queue age/depth (aggregated across routes) for the hard block, and I added per-route queue depth as “advisory” in the audit details only. Miles Thornton (review): What prevents a stale capacity signal from green-lighting failover during a telemetry outage? Benji: Added max_signal_staleness_s (default 30s) and an explicit STALE_SIGNAL failure reason. If stale, we block (or in observe-only, record). Irene Choi (review): For edge apply, are we actually calling the provider in prod precheck? That’s risky. Benji: In prod it’s a dry-run validate call; actual changes happen only once state machine starts progressive steps and only after approvals/guardrails. In staging we do the real call to test the integration path. Harish Reddy (review): The min headroom threshold (15%) might be too high for some dedicated pools. Can we make it tier-aware? Benji: I made thresholds configurable by capacity class (hosted/shared vs dedicated) and added defaults. Tier-aware routing is in ENG-2846, but we can already set per-pool overrides via config. Aisha Bello (review): Please add a metric for “precheck failed but overridden” so we can audit unsafe actions. Benji: Added failover_precheck_override_total{reason_code=...} and included the override actor in the audit log. Ethan Park (review): Any behavior changes when the flag is off? Benji: No state machine behavior changes; we only wire the precheck evaluation when the flag is enabled. When flag is off, current behavior remains. Mina Haddad (approval): Approved with the clarifications. Miles Thornton (approval): LGTM, tests look solid. Irene Choi (approval): Approved; staging behavior noted.
